A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HCEP framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic recovery experiments and image-classification, concept-recovery, runtime, and ablation results on ImageNet, ImageNette, and CIFAR-100.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative CLIP/GPT-5 interpretations of synset-difference embeddings.

M1.justification: The synset-difference dictionary, path-restricted beam search, least-squares updates, and downstream classifier remain. Hierarchical OMP is renamed HB-OMP and its pseudocode reorganized. The new textual interpretations are presented as an auxiliary qualitative analysis, rather than a changed classification procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic hierarchies, ImageNet, ImageNette, and CIFAR-100, retaining full-data and few-shot scenarios. The added WordNet interpretation examples examine existing concepts without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: OMP for synthetic recovery, and OMP, CBM, nearest neighbor, and hierarchical nearest neighbor for real-data comparisons. Newly cited sparse-autoencoder methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 revises the reported WordNet depth from 12 to 14; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Appendix F.2 adds a qualitative protocol using GPT-5 descriptions, CLIP nearest-neighbor retrieval, and summarization. Existing sample counts, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.2 and Tables 1 and 3 examine whether synset-difference vectors have meaningful textual interpretations, showing retrieved concepts and generated summaries. Existing beam-size ablations, runtime analyses, and geometric-condition checks are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The reporting practice remains point estimates and descriptive distributions.

E6.justification: Orthogonality histograms are updated, notably replacing v1's duplicated ImageNet/CIFAR-100 histogram with a distinct CIFAR-100 distribution in v3 Figure 15. Tables 1 and 3 add qualitative interpretation results. Existing classification and runtime results are retained; v3 Figure 9 reproduces all scores from v1 Table 1.

T1.justification: Targeted revisions change Proposition 3.3's bound from d >= L+b to d >= L+b-1, replace the matrix-infinity-norm ERC definition with a maximum of column l1 norms, and revise the path decomposition to include the terminal node. However, Appendix E.1 still retains d >= L+b. The classical sparse-recovery background subsection is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: geometric conditions for hierarchical embeddings, hierarchical sparse pursuit, improved concept recovery with competitive classification, and stronger few-shot performance. Rewriting does not materially change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds an explanation of few-shot gains through averaging embeddings rather than learning concept predictors, together with reduced spurious selections from path restrictions. Figure 8's caption qualifies superiority at hierarchy-depth sparsity. Existing geometry, hierarchy-quality, computational, and outlier limitations move to Appendix C.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, the CIFAR-100 taxonomy-generation prompt, and the residual-description prompt. Appendix F documents GPT-5, CLIP retrieval, and top-10 concepts for the new analysis. Existing backbone, optimizer, learning-rate, epoch, batch-size, and beam-size disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds hierarchical compositional work, while Appendix A discusses sparse-autoencoder studies, including Costa, Olson, and Zaigrajew, and distinguishes HCEP's explicit semantic dictionary. References associated with the removed generic sparse-recovery review disappear. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting affects the introduction, preliminaries, method explanation, experiments, and proofs. Related work is redistributed into Section 2.3 and Appendix A, limitations move to Appendix C, and the sparse-recovery tutorial is removed while OMP explanation moves into the main text.

P2.justification: The ImageNet score table becomes a three-panel bar chart, four tables add interpretation examples and prompts, and six algorithm displays are consolidated into three main-text algorithms. Geometry plots are rearranged, diagrams and captions revised, and appendix displays substantially redistributed.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, the revised ERC definition, replacement of the duplicated CIFAR-100 histogram, and added interpretation examples and reproducibility disclosures improve assessability. Gains are limited by the inconsistent dimension bounds in Proposition 3.3 and Appendix E.1, and by replacing exact tabulated scores with unlabeled bars. The central empirical evidence remains unchanged.
